stem.en: Hydrogen and oxygen can sit mixed in a balloon for years. Touch a flame to it and it explodes. Kabir says "the flame gives the gas its energy". What is the better account?

text.en: The reaction is downhill and releases far more energy than the flame supplied. The flame only lifted a few collisions over the hump; the heat they released lifted the rest.
The flame supplies all the energy of the explosion.

feedback.en: A match's heat is tiny compared with the bang. Almost all of it came from the hydrogen and oxygen falling to water.

text.en: The balloon was holding the gas back.

feedback.en: The gas is mixed inside the balloon and could react at any moment. It does not, because nothing is over the hump.

text.en: Hydrogen and oxygen are not really downhill.

feedback.en: Downhill things go by themselves only if there is no hump. This hump is high enough to hold the reaction for years.

explanation.en: Separate the hump from the fall. The match pays for the hump, once. The fall pays for everything after.
